what: Five Below is an American discount chain aimed at teenagers and their parents, selling toys, snacks, beauty, tech accessories and seasonal goods, mostly priced under $5.
customers: Teenagers, pre-teens and parents, in about 1,900 stores across the United States.
money: merchandise sold in its own stores
moat: A price point and an assortment aimed at an age group other retailers serve badly, refreshed constantly so there is a reason to come back.
risks: Almost everything is imported from China, so tariffs hit the cost base directly
Shrink, meaning theft, rose sharply and forced changes to store layouts
Chinese online sellers compete directly at the same price points
opportunities: Revenue grew from $2.8B to $4.8B in four years while opening hundreds of stores
$932M of cash and a 7.5% net margin, high for a discount retailer
Analysts see about 31% upside, with 23 covering the stock
watch: Comparable store sales and the gross margin, which shows the tariff impact.
